groups.name: valuation-inputs
groups.reason: Valuation methodology (D-18, D-19): the near-term growth anchor became the median of four methods with its range shown, the terminal rule is labelled a house convention, WACC inputs are disclosed by source and observation date, free cash flow is reported net of stock-based compensation, the enterprise-value bridge is explicit, and an own-history multiple is a rank among N quarters. Fair value, the score drivers reading those inputs, and the disclaimer text move with them.

after.name: free cash flow, SBC treatment
after.basis: Stock-based compensation is expensed inside the EBIT this DCF projects, so it is never added back here; the reported free-cash-flow metric subtracts it as well (house default). The FCFF path derives from revenue, EBIT margin and reinvestment, not from the free-cash-flow metric, so the two are consistent but not the same series. Reported free cash flow as of 2025-12-31: 1800000000 before SBC → 1550000000 after subtracting SBC of 250000000.

after.note: Dilution from outstanding awards: diluted 205000000 vs basic 200000000 weighted-average shares as of 2025-12-31 — a 2.5% overhang. Options, RSUs and convertibles that are antidilutive in a loss year are excluded from the diluted count by the filer, so a loss-making issuer's overhang understates the award pool.

deltas.after: Free cash flow = operating cash flow + capital expenditure (FMP capex negative), MINUS stock-based compensation (house default: SBC is a cash-equivalent operating expense settled in shares, not a genuine add-back — Damodaran, "Stock Based Compensation: The Elephant in the Room"). Both the before- and after-SBC figures are reported; years with no disclosed SBC are unadjusted and say so. TWO conversion ratios are published and never conflated: FCF-after-SBC / net income is the house-default headline, and FCF-before-SBC / net income is the ratio the balance-sheet grading band was calibrated on and the one that is GRADED — grading the after-SBC ratio on that band would charge the same expense twice, because SBC as a percentage of free cash flow is already a scored metric.

deltas.before: Value creation (ROIC−WACC) and accounting integrity (Piotroski, Altman, accruals, Beneish).
deltas.after: Value creation (ROIC−WACC, dropped where the route suppresses it — financial routes are costed on equity alone) and accounting integrity (Piotroski, weighted by the share of its nine signals that were evaluable; plus Altman — banded after an affine map of the variant's zones onto the original 1.81/2.99 scale, which is the value the altmanZOriginalScale driver carries — accruals and Beneish where the route computes them — all three are withheld for financial classifications, whose balance sheets those models were not estimated on).
House heuristic: no SIC code available — manufacturer status inferred from sector/industry strings (non-manufacturer → Z″).
X5 (sales/TA) is dropped by the Z″ model to remove industry asset-turnover effects.

DEPI: rate built from combined depreciation AND amortisation over (D&A + net PP&E) — the statements do not separate depreciation; Beneish's index is on depreciation of PP&E alone, so an acquisitive issuer's intangible amortisation moves this index for reasons unrelated to depreciation policy (research §2.1).
TATA uses the cash-flow construction (NI from continuing ops − CFO)/TA_t (Hribar–Collins 2002); balance-sheet construction reported as diagnostic only.
Diagnostic balance-sheet TATA uses shortTermDebt as a proxy for current maturities of LTD (broader — includes notes payable).
The model detects overstatement, not understatement — a very negative M does not prove conservative accounting.
ΔLEVER: prior-year average TA proxied by end-of-year TA (no t−2 balance sheet) — annotated proxy.

groups.name: valuation-review-repairs
groups.reason: Repairs the fresh-context review of D-18 and D-19 asked for. The graded free-cash-flow conversion returns to the before-stock-compensation ratio its band was calibrated on, so the expense is charged to the score once rather than twice; the price-to-free-cash-flow multiple says which definition it uses; the number of observations behind an own-history rank is published beside it; the per-year WACC shortfall reaches the missing-data manifest; the terminal-growth cap calls itself a house convention like the terminal ROIC rule beside it; and the enterprise-value bridge stops removing a lease liability it cannot split into its operating and finance halves. Twelve leaves left this list in the same change, returning to the audited values, which is what those last two repairs were for.

groups.reason: The 2026-09-06 audit of the returns and capital modules (D-25). groups.name: growth-anchor-span-window
groups.reason: DEMO has two years of annual revenue history, so its 3y and 5y revenue CAGRs both measure 2.00 years. The DCF growth anchor used to count that one two-year rate twice, as '3y revenue CAGR 9.11%' and '5y revenue CAGR 9.11%', beside the regression. Under D-39 a CAGR whose measured span differs from its window by more than 0.25 years (grading's tolerance, now growth.ts windowCagr) is excluded from the anchor and listed as unavailable with its span.
